purpose: Registration fragment for the Airlock Plan application: the app's own MCP binding plus the owner binding of Universal UserIO, kept in sync with the live tool set. Merges into integrations/airlock-apps/apps.json; the registry itself is read-only for this task.

principal.note: The binding reuses the owner's own Universal UserIO resource; no per-user member credential exists for it (agent_mcp_member_credentials holds 0 rows platform-wide).

platform_rule.text: binding.user_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM CASE WHEN need.binding_mode='shared' THEN NULL ELSE $1::uuid END AND (m.owner_principal_id = creator.id OR EXISTS (resource_grants with 'use' for creator))
platform_rule.consequence: A shared MCP resource resolves only while its owner_principal_id equals the binding creator (binding.created_by_user_id), or the creator holds a 'use' grant.
platform_rule.verified_by: read-only SELECT: resource 365c1a4b owner_principal_id=5e438326 and both bindings (airlockplan c2abb3bf, universal-userio 54968a2c) created_by_user_id=5e438326 -> the rule holds for both.

mcp_resource.name: Universal UserIO
mcp_resource.shared_with: the same resource backs the universal-userio app binding userio_owner (54968a2c); re-keying it rotates the owner-side credential for both, exactly the step the universal-userio-oleg fragment prescribes for the owner side

notes: The app container is idle-reaped by the platform ('stopping idle container' in the backend log). It is reconciled again on the next admitted request or with POST /api/v1/agents/{id}/start; the agent token lives in the container environment, so a probe that needs the token must start the container first.

The app's own operation allowlist (apps.json operations) still lists only the airlock_* operations; the platform-level userio_owner binding is independent of that list. Exposing userio.* through the app's own service_read tool would need an apps.json change, which was out of scope here.
The go.mod/go.sum/test migration lives in the shared integrations/airlock-apps source, so every app uploaded from it inherits the SDK 0.8 pin; re-uploads of the other apps pick it up.

A dedicated airlockplan_oleg binding would need the plan MCP token on the server (write-only in the platform credential store).
